title: Introduce dissector groups.
description:
Dissector groups are used to group dissectors together which has similar
use cases in order to make it easier to dissable protocols not
interesting for the current use case.
Initialy only the group Games is defined.
 - While at it add description of some dissectors, found google.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • cc2a0e3d - Introduce dissector groups.
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22408/diffs?diff_id=1574600031&start_sha=9b5ddad9249d86abec60a5f15b17f5b64d36d1f5)

Like the idea of groups and this is a good start.  I don't like some of the changes to disable some of the existing heuristics by default (more so previous MRs).  If they have a "magic number" or a "distinct series of bytes", I think they should be allowed to be enabled by default (and those changes should be reverted).  Maybe that can be done at the same time that they are assigned a group for easier (user) disabling.

 /** Structure for information about a protocol */
 typedef struct _protocol protocol_t;
 
+
+/**
+ * Protocol group enum used to group protoclols with a similar purpose together.
+ * Primary usage to be able to dissable/enable a group of protocols
+ * as not beeing relevant for a type of trace. E.g game protocol is of no use to you
+ * in a production network. Unless looking for gamers...
+ */
+
+typedef enum {
+    PROTOCOL_GROUP_NONE = 0,     /**< Not grouped*/
+    PROTOCOL_GROUP_GAMES,        /**< Protocols used by games */
+    PROTOCOL_GROUP_MAX,
+} protocol_group_t;
+
+
+/** Function to get the group of a protocol
+ * @param protocol the protocol in question
+*/
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC int proto_get_group(const protocol_t* protocol);
+
+/** Function to get the group name of a protocol group
+ * @param protocol the protocol in question
+*/
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC const char* proto_get_group_name(const protocol_t* protocol);
